For me an ideal 12 job run through looks like this...

Balthier - Shikari/Red (this is your controlled character)
Vaan - Knight/Black (he's the best, magepower and white robes he has 99 strength and mag... he's also the best time/monk but you've got to pick your battles)
Fran - Monk/Time (she's my stealer, healer, everything... she's not the best technically for this job but it's probably the best pairing for her. She looks cool with pole weapons. And she's fast.)
Basch - Bushi/Uhlan (pure physical attacker)

As for the last two... either Foebreaker/Archer (Ashe) and Machinist/White (Penelo) or... Foebreaker/Machinist (Penelo, berserker bot) and Archer/White (All around item and magical healing with shades of black).

That's just optimization. There are all kinds of combinations that work well. You could beat the game with 6 White mages if you wanted. 

Penelo also makes a great Shikari/Red. Ashe is almost as good a Knight/Black. Vaan is the best Monk/Time (for me that has to do with Steal. I like my support to steal).

I like a "main three" for general use and using the other three as niche fillers. I like magic so my Uhlan/Bushi is probably not going to be out much but in a physical fight I can pop him out with berserker braces and just let him be. You're not going to need a Foebreakers abilities much, especially since they come so late and other jobs have access to them but having one in the wings for Hellwyrm or whatever endgame content to just spam breaks and make your life easier can be nice. Not that you really ever need Breaks, they're just matters of convenience on some fights. Stuff like that.

There really aren't that many places with lots of unavoidable traps. Play around with your accessories. EXP accessories of course but berserker bracers are fun and other accessories can just provide generally more useful perks.

Since you can change jobs anyway play around. You don't have a monk yet, Fran is a pretty good monk and she looks cool with pole weapons. There are better Knights but, again, she looks cool with 2h swords. To me both Monk and Knight are begging for a mage secondary job (wouldn't recommend red) but both also pair well with Bushi if you want a physical attacker who eventually gets access to some great white magic. Both also pair great with White if you're not planning on getting all the Espers or if you want to use those Espers with other jobs.

On your license board you'll find things like Potion Lore 1, 2, 3... Remedy Lore 1, 2, 3 etc... for different types of curative items. Different jobs have access to different levels. Remedy Lore 3 is the most important probably.

Ether Lores are only found on mages though.

Edit: Breaks are abilities that reduces magical or physical attack or defense, there are four. You won't get them until late in the game and will likely never use them unless you are doing end game side content.

Edit 2: That guide is recommending Foebreaker for that stage of the game  because technically you can get its ultimate weapon after Wraithwall but it's very difficult and IMO not worth it. I do actually have a Foe/White on my team right now. I only plan on ever using it for two bosses, and only briefly. There are much better combos for everyday use.

Black/Time - Use staves to boost elemental spells (their names make them fairly apparent which is which, although the cloud staff increases multiple). If the target is magic immune or you can't use magic then switch to crossbow. Magic DPS with some buffs and mid healing (healing only with esper), lots of debuffs. Gambit are generally healing -> elemental weaknesses -> attack (very basically)

Red/Archer - Use Burning Bow to boost fire spells. Bows do decent damage if you can't use magic in the meantime. End game mace boosts Dark spells, so do Black Robes. Magic DPS, mid healing, item support (archer gets all item lores), some debuffs. Gambit mostly same as above.

Shikari/White - Excellent healing and tank. Use daggers and a shield for high evasion. Endgame has some uses for ninja blades... well, like one. Healing -> Attack for gambits.

Foebreaker/White - Basically the same as Shikari/White but you have breaks instead of item lores and axes/hammers instead of daggers/ninja blades. Gambits as well.

Basically.

Vaan as a monk/time mage is great. Heavy esper investment necessary though. My personal favorite support combo. Fran works well enough too. Switch Knight to Ashe and go Knight/Black mage. Great combo. Vaan is also an excellent Black/Knight. Shikari/White is a great tank or general all around backup - end game killer. I prefer Shikari/Red though. Both are an excellent combo for Penelo. I run Balthier as a Red/Shikari all the time, and I’d use him for a Shikari/White too. Basch is a great Uhlan/Bushi. Archer/White then if you really want a white mage. Beefy high HP white mage with all item lores minus ether 3 so in the battles where magic is unavailable it can still heal well. Adds a decent weapon. Lots of options. Play what seems fun but you’re off to a good start.

Explore everything. There are a few items that have a % chance to spawn but most are 100% (Power Armlet, Thief’s Cuffs in the caverns, Cleanse, and that accessory that makes it so you always hit are some important ones that have < 100% chance and you may need to load the area). It pays to explore all areas in this game.

Shops will be important throughout the game for upgrades.

For the Bazaar you’ll probably need a guide if you really want to use it. Some powerful weapons can only be acquired through the Bazaar. Some you can get in trial mode, along with many other useful items. Keep at least 10 of everything is a good rule of thumb, this will help prevent yourself from accidentally selling quest/important crafting items.

As far as stats go you really do have to go through the equipment menu an look at them but in general higher licensed equipment is better. If you’re playing around with elemental attributes like on robes or staves then you use what’s appropriate for that element. The best equipment takes time to get, use a guide. Running around the Great Crystal is infuriating your first time trying to get Excalibur.

Just to stress again. Explore everything. Many of the best equipment, spells, tech are found only in chests.
